docs.title: Anhbnb — Lodging Booking Backend
docs.text:
Backend project | Completed · Aug – Sep 2026

Aspect Details Project Backend for a lodging booking service, built individually. Booking & Concurrency REST APIs with Node.js and Express. PostgreSQL transactions and row-level locking manage concurrent room bookings, with Redis for caching and coordination. Events & Search A transactional outbox with Debezium CDC and Kafka updates Elasticsearch search indexes and invalidates caches through idempotent consumers. Testing APIs tested with Postman; unit, integration and end-to-end tests for booking flows and event processing. Technologies Used Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Debezium, Elasticsearch, Docker Compose, Postman Repository github.com/tertueanhvu/Anhbnb--backend-project

docs.title: Divvy Data Platform
docs.text:
← Back to Portfolio

Status: in progress

The server-track code is implemented and its deployment is in progress. The cloud track is designed but not yet built.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
An end-to-end data engineering project (team project) on Divvy, Chicago's bike-share system. It combines:

  • a monthly trip batch pipeline: Spark ETL into an S3-compatible lake, then PostgreSQL and dbt marts;
  • live station status collected from the public GBFS feed;
  • near-real-time alerts for stations that run out of bikes or docks (Kafka + Flink).

Every step is an idempotent CLI with a fixed exit-code contract.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Track What Status A · Server (Docker Compose) Everything runs as Docker Compose services on one Linux host: PostgreSQL 18, RustFS (S3-compatible lake), the Spark / Great Expectations / dbt tools image, the GBFS poller, Kafka, Flink and the alert consumer. Code complete · server deployment in progress B · Cloud (GCP) Cloud Storage lake, Cloud Run Jobs running the same tools image, BigQuery + dbt, Cloud Scheduler. Architecture only — future implementation

docs.title: Data flows
docs.text:
Batch — trip files (monthly).

  1. Download the ZIP and check its integrity, header and row count.
  2. Transform it with Spark into typed Parquet in the lake. Rows that cannot be parsed go to a quarantine area with a reason; nothing is dropped silently.
  3. Validate it with Great Expectations.
  4. Load it into PostgreSQL with DELETE partition + COPY in one transaction, and reconcile row counts.
  5. Build the dbt models.

Live — station status. A poller reads the GBFS v2.3 station_status feed every 2 minutes with conditional requests and stores each new feed version as a raw file in the lake. An hourly job compacts those files into a snapshot plus change events, and dbt turns them into station state intervals.

Streaming — alerts. The poller also publishes every station of every feed version to Kafka. A Flink SQL job uses 10-minute event-time windows that slide every 2 minutes and emits EMPTY / LOW / FULL / NEARLY_FULL alerts. A consumer keeps each alert's open → updated → resolved lifecycle in PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
Mart Answers mart_trip_analytics Trip trends, members vs casual riders, e-bike share, dockless trips mart_station_demand Busiest stations, hour × weekday patterns, net flow (arrivals − departures) mart_station_availability Share of observed time a station was empty or full, and when it happens fct_station_alert_episodes History of real-time shortage / surplus alerts

Tech stack: Python 3.11 · Apache Spark (PySpark) · RustFS (S3 API) + Parquet · PostgreSQL · dbt Core · Great Expectations · Apache Kafka · Apache Flink SQL · Docker Compose

docs.title: MEWA — Budgeted Vietnamese–English Legal Evidence Retrieval
docs.text:
← Back to Portfolio

Status: in development

The Phase 1 pipeline is implemented. The first run on real data is in progress, so there are no results yet.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Answering a Vietnamese legal question often needs evidence that is not in Vietnamese: the English version of a Vietnamese law, a treaty Viet Nam is bound by, or an EU regulation that a Vietnamese decree implements. MEWA (Marginal Evidence Work Allocation) is the retrieval layer of a cross-lingual legal RAG system. For each question, before searching, it decides how to split a fixed ANN search budget between a Vietnamese index and an English index.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text:
• Evidence is split across languages. About 15.6k Vietnamese legal documents are listed with an English version on TVPL, and treaty and EU law exists mainly in English. Searching only Vietnamese misses this evidence; searching everything for every question multiplies the cost.
  • Questions differ. Most are fully answered by Vietnamese law, and a few need English sources. A fixed split wastes budget on both groups.
  • A single multilingual index is not a fix. Its inverted lists tend to be language-pure, so a global probe order under a tight budget ends up favouring one language.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
For each question, choose how many IVF lists to probe in each index, pVI, pEN ∈ {0, 1, 2, 4, …, 64}:

argmax  Û(q, p_VI, p_EN)   subject to   W_VI(p_VI) + W_EN(p_EN) ≤ B
  • W is the exact fine-scan work: the summed size of the probed lists, known before the scan.
  • U is Recall@10 of evidence after union → rerank → grouping by article. A Vietnamese article and its English translation count as one piece of evidence.
  • Û comes from a gradient-boosted model that sees only pre-search signals: coarse centroid scores, list sizes, the query embedding and lexical cues. The best feasible allocation is found by exact enumeration over the 63 options.
  • Baselines: static splits, separable / additive and ranking models, a single global index, and the per-question oracle.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Offline: builds a bilingual evidence pool with judgments from Vietnamese laws, legal Q&A, benchmarks and EUR-Lex. The pool is encoded with BGE-M3 and indexed in one Faiss IVF index per language. Searching at every probe depth gives a utility table per question, on which the utility model is trained.
  • Online: for each question, MEWA predicts the utility of all 63 allocations and picks the best one within budget B. It then scans both indexes, reranks, and merges a Vietnamese article with its English translation into a single piece of evidence. Answer generation is Phase 2.

Data: Vietnamese legal documents and legal Q&A from TVPL, Zalo / ALQAC benchmarks for out-of-domain tests, and EUR-Lex for English evidence.

Tech stack: Python · Faiss IVF · BGE-M3 · bge-reranker-v2-m3 · VinAI Translate · scikit-learn · Qwen2.5 on vLLM

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
• Research plan and utility-model formulation
  • Phase 1 pipeline: data → indexes → utility model → evaluation
  • Pilot run on real data (in progress)
  • Full run, final evaluation, ablations
  • Phase 2: legal retriever adaptation and answer generation
